research: https://developers.googleblog.com/en/how-to-prompt-gemini-2-5-flash-image-generation-for-the-best-results/ — Google's own guidance: describe the scene as a narrative paragraph (subject, setting, light, camera), not a keyword list; 'photorealistic' plus concrete action and lighting.

https://www.atlabs.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-prompting-guide — Nano Banana 2 responds strongly to named photographic language (film stock, lens, lighting); be explicit about environment and light or it fills gaps with glossy defaults.
https://www.hooked.so/prompts/nano-banana?page=3 — practitioner snapshot prompts work by naming the flaws: grain, motion blur, harsh or no flash, tilted messy composition, cheap camera.
https://localbanana.io/docs/realistic-photos-guide — realism comes from naming the camera/film simulation and imperfections rather than 'high quality' words.

https://www.photrio.com/forum/threads/cinestill-800t-whats-it-all-about.166552/ — tungsten-balanced/cross-processed cine film under fluorescent goes cold and greenish, with halation round bright lights: the reference's teal cast.
https://gridfiti.com/cinestill-vs-portra — daylight stocks (Portra) push warm; the cold blue-teal look at night comes from fluorescent tubes on cheap or tungsten stock, slightly underexposed.

https://photofocus.com/found/photographing-the-mood-and-unease-of-liminal-spaces/ — ordinary transit places (storefronts, car parks) turn eerie once empty; frame to suggest being alone; lighting makes the mood.
https://howtofilmschool.com/dictionary/negative-space/ — horror leaves a suspiciously empty part of the frame where the viewer expects something; the mind fills it.
https://www.slashfilm.com/578134/fractured/ — The Invisible Man frames empty rooms and doorways as if occupied: the camera lingers on nothing.
https://www.studiobinder.com/blog/liminal-space-movies/ — one-point perspective corridors and doorways-within-doorways as thresholds of dread.
https://fliki.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-prompting-guide — write prose sentences, not keyword lists; naming a film stock (Portra 400, Cinestill 800T) and the light source steers the rendering

https://budgetpixel.com/blog/analog-neon-prompting-1990s-cyberpunk-street-photography — anti-CGI phrasing that works: heavy organic grain, halation round bright sources, 'no digital render, no smooth plastic surfaces'
https://www.imagine.art/blogs/nano-banana-2-prompt-guide — name camera and lens; describe flaws (tilt, soft focus, underexposure) to get a candid snapshot instead of a staged image

https://brooklynfilmcamera.com/blogs/guides/after-dark-the-best-film-stocks-for-cinematic-night-photography — Portra is flatter and neutral, Cinestill/400-speed consumer stocks saturate; night stocks are pushed and grainy
https://madssmidstrup.squarespace.com/blog/night-photography-with-cinestill-800t — fluorescent and neon light on tungsten/consumer film render cold, blue-green, with tubes blowing out and halation

https://www.photrio.com/forum/threads/help-with-options-for-low-light-night-time-street-photography.216371 — underexposed night colour negative gives a green-teal cast and muddy, lifted shadows (the reference's look)
https://www.mentalfloss.com/science/psychology/why-are-liminal-spaces-creepy — an ordinary place built for people feels wrong when shown empty and out of context
https://photofocus.com/found/capturing-the-eerie-atmosphere-of-liminal-spaces/ — liminal eeriness comes from flat fluorescent light, emptiness and a place that should be in use
https://theasc.com/article/shot-craft-halloween-horrors-creating-visual-cues-to-foster-fright/ — leave a suspiciously empty part of the frame where the eye expects something; edge-of-frame tension
https://www.denofgeek.com/?p=68353 — It Follows / Sinister: negative space and dark depths behind the subject make an unseen presence felt
https://fliki.ai/blog/nano-banana-2-prompting-guide — write Nano Banana 2 prompts as full prose sentences, not comma-separated tag lists
https://carat.im/en/prompt-gallery/film-grain-photo — community film-look prompts name a specific stock/35mm camera and spell out grain and halation around bright areas

https://budgetpixel.com/blog/analog-neon-prompting-1990s-cyberpunk-street-photography — snapshot realism comes from listing imperfections: tilted, messy framing, motion blur, harsh shadows, documentary handheld feel, avoid HDR/AI glow

https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/ai-machine-learning/ultimate-prompting-guide-for-nano-banana — Google's own guide covers Nano Banana 2; use photographic vocabulary (camera, lens, light); earlier words weigh more, so lead with the film look

https://www.uniquephoto.com/photoinsider/cinestill-800t-vs-kodak-portra-800-which-fast-color-film-for-night-photography — fast colour stocks at night: tungsten-balanced 800T turns light cool and blooms light sources (halation); Portra 800 warmer and punchier
https://www.adorama.com/CS800135.html — 800T is balanced for incandescent, not fluorescent, so fluorescent shops render off-colour (green/teal), which is exactly the reference's cast
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liminal_space_(aesthetic) — empty everyday places become eerie through the absence of the people who should be there; fluorescent light and odd angles push it
https://www.slashfilm.com/578134/fractured/ — The Invisible Man weaponises negative space: the audience distrusts any empty part of the frame
https://nofilmschool.com/ways-horror-likes-scare-its-audience — a door ajar, a reflection in a dark surface, a suspiciously empty patch of frame keep the viewer hunting for an unseen threat

notes.PR: All five are no-people, no-brand, available-light colour-film snapshots in the reference's teal fluorescent look. Only PR2-e echoes the doorway, and reverses it (from inside looking out). The unseen force is carried by negative space: a half-open stockroom door with one tube out (c), an empty stool behind the counter (d), a door ajar on its own (e). Price text '50p' is asked for in b, d and e; check it renders exactly. No flash in any prompt (the reference has none).
notes.CL: Beat B (climb) is £1 then £5, the shop getting darker each time. Ids a/b lean on £1 and some failing light; c/d/e are £5 and darker, so they can be cut in that order. Only CL2-e echoes the reference's pavement-through-the-doorway framing (brief allows one). Every prompt names a consumer colour film at night, available light only, grain, cold teal fluorescent cast, and the unseen presence as an empty space/moved object/dead light, never a figure. Price text is quoted exactly ('£1', '£5'); check every still for misspelt or extra prices and reroll if wrong. No brands: packets and signs are asked to be invented or unreadable. If Nano Banana 2 drifts glossy, the anti-CGI sentence is the one to strengthen, not the scene.
notes.FO: Beat C, £50. The force is shown only by its traces: a price on its own, a till printer running with nobody there, blank uncut banknote sheets on the floor (the printer's leavings, never the printer's owner), an open stockroom door with light inside. No person, no face, no hand in any prompt. FO2-e is the one prompt that echoes the reference's doorway framing. Price text: every label is "£50" except the till ("£50.00") and the purple bar in FO2-e ("£12", its own rising price; change if the Fredo ladder uses another number). Banknotes in FO2-d are specified with no readable design to avoid currency-reproduction blocks; if Flow blocks it, swap to 'blank paper sheets fresh from a printer'. If the model drifts glossy, move 'cheap 35mm colour film, grainy, underexposed' even earlier and add 'not HDR'.

stills.look: Street wide: the only lit shop on the row
stills.prompt: A vertical amateur snapshot on cheap colour negative film, taken at night from across a damp British terraced street. A small corner shop glows alone, the only lit window on the whole row; every house around it is dark. A hand-written paper sign is taped inside the glass, unreadable. Fluorescent tubes spill a cold blue-teal light onto the wet pavement, a far-off sodium streetlamp gives a weak orange. The shop door is propped open and nobody is inside or outside. Slightly underexposed, heavy grain, soft focus, faint halation round the tubes, horizon a little tilted. Unglamorous and lonely, like a photo taken walking home. No people, no brands. Thanks.

stills.look: Shelf insert: one loaf, label reads 50p
stills.prompt: A close vertical snapshot on grainy colour film, no flash, of a low metal shelf in a cramped British corner shop at night. One loaf of plain white sliced bread in a clear unbranded plastic bag sits alone; the rest of the shelf is bare. A white shelf-edge price label clipped in front of it reads "50p" in black marker. A single fluorescent tube overhead casts a cold blue-green tint, and the back of the shelf sinks into murky shadow. Soft focus, slightly underexposed, dust on the plastic, a crooked handheld frame. Ordinary, cheap, and quietly unsettling, as if the price is a trap. Thanks.

stills.look: Down the aisle: stockroom door half open, one tube out
stills.prompt: A vertical amateur photograph on cheap ISO 400 colour film at night, taken from the front end of the single narrow aisle of a British corner shop, looking straight down it to the back. Shelves of tins, crisps and loo roll on both sides, packets unreadable. At the far end a stockroom door stands half open onto pure black. The fluorescent tube nearest the back is dead, so the far end sits in gloom while the near end is lit teal-white. The aisle is empty, yet it feels as if someone has just stepped out of it. Grain, soft focus, slight shake blur, underexposed. Thanks.

stills.look: At the counter: bread, coins, empty stool
stills.prompt: A vertical snapshot on grainy colour film, from the customer's side of a British corner shop counter late at night. On the scuffed counter: a loaf of plain white sliced bread, a small handwritten card propped against it reading "50p", a few copper and silver coins, and a small unbranded purple chocolate bar. Behind the counter nobody, just an empty stool still turning slightly, a pulled-down metal shutter, a newspaper rack with unreadable headlines, a UK three-pin plug socket with a kettle lead. Fluorescent tubes blow out at the top of frame, cold teal cast, dark corners, soft focus. Unstaged, ordinary, and wrong. Thanks.

stills.look: Reverse doorway: from inside, door ajar onto black street
stills.prompt: A vertical amateur snapshot on cheap colour film at night, taken from inside a small British corner shop looking out through its open glass front door at an empty dark street. The door has swung ajar on its own. In the foreground a dirty rubber doormat and a plastic bread crate holding a single white sliced loaf with a sticker reading "50p"; a wire spinner rack of crisps at the edge; a handwritten paper sign taped to the glass, seen backwards. Outside is black, one distant streetlamp, wet pavement. Teal fluorescent light inside, grain, soft focus, underexposed, slight motion blur. Something just came in. Thanks.

stills.look: Street wide, half the tubes dead
stills.prompt: A vertical 9:16 amateur snapshot on cheap 400-speed colour negative film, taken at night from across a wet terraced British street, looking at a small corner shop on the end of the row. The shop is the only lit thing, but half its ceiling tubes are dead, so the left side of the window is black and the right side glows cold blue-green. A handwritten fluorescent card in the window reads "BREAD £1". Newspaper board, wheelie bin, a lamp post at the frame edge. The open doorway is dark and empty. Underexposed, heavy grain, soft focus, halation round the tubes, muddy teal shadows, slightly tilted. No people, no brands, no digital render. Thanks.

Vertical 9:16 close snapshot on grainy consumer colour film, flash off, inside a cramped British corner shop at night. A low metal shelf of plain white sliced bread in clear plastic bags, most of the row gone: one loaf left at the end, a gap where the others were, crumbs on the shelf. A white shelf-edge label in sharp focus reads "£1". Above it a fluorescent tube flickers, caught half-bright, throwing a cold green-blue cast. The aisle behind falls off into soft blur and shadow, deeper than it should be. Off-centre, slightly underexposed, lifted murky blacks, visible grain. Unbranded packets, no people. Not polished, not CGI. Thanks.

stills.look: Aisle to the back, lights out in stages
stills.prompt: Vertical 9:16 night photograph on cheap colour negative film, standing at the front of a narrow British corner-shop aisle and looking straight down it. Only the front tube is still on; each one after is off, so the aisle fades step by step into near-black at the back, where the stockroom door stands open a hand's width. Crisps and tins on cluttered shelves, unbranded. On the floor halfway down, a single loaf of white sliced bread lies dropped, a price sticker reading "£5". Cold teal fluorescent cast, blown highlights, thick grain, soft focus, slightly crooked framing. Empty of people, but the dark end feels occupied. No digital sheen. Thanks.

A vertical 9:16 candid snapshot on grainy 35mm colour film, at night, across the counter of a small British corner shop. Nobody behind it: an empty stool, a cash register drawer left open and empty, a scratchcard stand with invented unreadable cards, a radio. On the counter a small open box of unbranded purple chocolate bars, a sticker on the box reading "£5". One white loaf waits on the counter as if someone set it down and left. Above, the single working tube buzzes cold green-blue; the doorway to the back room behind the counter is pitch black. Underexposed, muddy shadows, halation, grain, soft focus. No people, no logos, not glossy. Thanks.

stills.look: Pavement through the door, almost dark
stills.prompt: Vertical 9:16 amateur night snapshot on cheap colour film, from the pavement looking in through the open glass door of a British corner shop. The shop is nearly dark now: one flickering tube at the back and the glow of a drinks fridge. On the rubber doormat a wire spinner rack has turned to face the door. A handwritten paper sign taped to the glass reads "BREAD £5", the £1 beneath it scribbled out. The inner door has swung half shut on its own. Deep murky teal-black, the fridge light blooming, coarse grain, soft focus, underexposed, slightly skewed. Nobody there. No brands, nothing staged or digital. Thanks.

stills.look: Insert: the £50 shelf label, nothing else left
stills.prompt: A vertical amateur snapshot on cheap 35mm colour negative film, pushed at night, heavy grain, slightly soft focus, underexposed, a cold teal-green fluorescent cast. Close-up of a bread shelf in a small British corner shop: one plain white sliced loaf left on a bare metal shelf, its paper shelf-edge price label reading exactly "£50" in black marker, older crossed-out prices beneath it. The fluorescent tube above is half dead, so the left of the frame falls into murky darkness. Crumbs, a torn plastic bag clip, dust. Flash not used, available light only, nobody in the shop. Thanks.

stills.look: Till printer spilling paper, empty counter
stills.prompt: A vertical night snapshot on grainy expired colour film, available light only, soft focus, blue-teal cast, blown-out fluorescent tubes. A cluttered British corner shop counter with no one behind it: an unbranded lottery stand, a newspaper rack, cigarette shutters closed. The small receipt printer beside the till is still running by itself, a long curling ribbon of paper spilling over the counter edge and piling on the lino floor. The till display glows green and reads "£50.00". A plain white sliced loaf sits waiting on the counter. The door to the back room behind is ajar, black inside. Candid, slightly crooked framing. Thanks.

stills.look: Street wide: the only lit shop on the terrace
stills.prompt: A vertical snapshot from across a wet British terraced street at 3am, cheap 35mm colour film, coarse grain, underexposed, cold teal shadows and green fluorescent glow. A tiny corner shop is the only lit window on the row; every house around it is dark. A hand-written card in the shop window reads "BREAD £50". The shop door stands open onto the empty pavement, warm-white light spilling across a puddle. No people, no cars moving, one sodium streetlamp out. The window display looks lived-in and ordinary, but the open door feels like an invitation. Slight camera shake, horizon a little tilted. Thanks.

stills.look: Convex mirror: the aisle watched from above
stills.prompt: A vertical night photograph on grainy colour negative film, amateur and underexposed, fluorescent light rendered sickly green-blue with soft halation. Looking up at a round convex security mirror in the corner of a cramped British corner shop. In the curved mirror the narrow aisle bends away, completely empty: snack racks, a lit drinks fridge, a bread shelf at the end with one loaf and a tiny label reading "£50". On the floor of the aisle, scattered blank uncut sheets of fresh paper banknotes with no readable design, as if dropped moments ago. No figure anywhere, only the sense someone just left. Thanks.

stills.look: Doorway at closing: sign, purple bar, back door open
stills.prompt: A vertical snapshot from the pavement through the open glass door of a small British corner shop at night, shot on cheap 35mm colour film, grainy, soft, underexposed, cold teal cast with overblown fluorescent tubes. Hand-printed paper sign taped to the door glass reads "BREAD £50". Inside: a wire spinner rack, a lit fridge, a wall fan, and at the far end the stockroom door wide open, a cold blue light pulsing from inside it. On the dirty doormat a small unbranded purple chocolate bar has fallen, its sticker reading "£12". The shop is empty yet feels occupied. Thanks.
